name: Terodiline

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market worldwide, first in 1991 — for heart harm

similar.name: Prenylamine
problems: Pulled from the market worldwide, first in 1989 — for heart harm

problems: Pulled from the market in United States and 9 other countries, first in 1987 — for nerve and brain harm

summary: A small computer program, not tests on human beings, rated Terodiline with a low score of 12 for liver risk and a medium score of 63 for heart risk [M]. Starting in 1991, the drug was taken off the market worldwide due to heart harm [3]. Similar drugs were also removed from markets, including Prenylamine worldwide in 1989 for heart harm, Mebanazine in the United Kingdom in 1975 for liver harm, and Phenylpropanolamine in the United States and nine other nations starting in 1987 for harm to the nervous system [3][4].
